notes.text: START Of UNIVERSE
The universe arguably began with the Big Bang.
Big Bang occurred around 13.79 billion years ago. (Age of Universe is 13.79 billion years)
Our galaxy, the Milky Way, formed about 13.6 billion years ago.
Edwin Hubble discovered the universe is expanding.
Milky Way is the galaxy that contains our Solar System.
It is a spiral galaxy.
The Milky Way appears as a faint white band in the night sky.
The name "Milky Way" comes from its milky appearance in the sky.
It contains 100-400 billion stars.
The Sun is located in the Orion Arm of the Milky Way.
The Solar System orbits the galactic center once every ~225 million years.
The center of the Milky Way has a supermassive black hole called Sagittarius A*.
Andromeda is the nearest galaxy to the Milky Way.
Milky Way and Andromeda are expected to collide in ~4.5 billion years.
Sun is a Yellow Dwarf star.
Mass of Sun is 1.98x10^30 Kg
Sun is mainly made of Hydrogen (74%) and Helium (24%) & Some heavy metals.
Sun's surface temperature is ~5,500°C.
Sun's core temperature is ~15 million °C.
Sunlight takes ~8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth.
Sun contains 99.86% of the mass of the Solar System.
Sun produces energy by nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium.
Sun's diameter is about 1.39 million kilometers.
Sun's age is estimated to be 4.6 billion years.
Sun is located ~150 million km (1 AU) from Earth.
Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.
Mercury's distance from Sun is ~58 million km.
Mercury is the smallest planet.
Mercury has no atmosphere (no air).
Mercury has no moons.
Mercury has the fastest revolution - 88 Earth days.
Venus is the hottest planet.
Venus is called the Morning and Evening Star.
Venus has the slowest rotation - 243 Earth days
Venus has no moons.
Only planet to rotate clockwise.
Earth is the only planet known to support life.
Age of Earth is 4.54 billion years
Exact shape of Earth is Oblate Spheroid
Shape of Earth's orbit around sun is Elliptical
Earth is the densest planet - 5.51 g/cm3.
Earth has one Moon (natural satellite).
Earth's diameter is approximately 12,742 km.
Earth's polar diameter is approximately 43 km shorter
Earth's equatorial radius is 6,378 km.
Earth's true/average radius is 6,371 km.
Earth's Circumference is 40,000 Km
Al-Biruni estimated Earth's radius to be 6,339.9 km (very close to actual).
Earth rotates on its axis once every 23 hours,56 minutes (sidereal day).
Earth's rotation speed at the equator is approx. 1,670 km/h (465 m/s).
Earth revolves around the Sun in 365.25 days.
Earth's orbital (revolution) speed is approx. 107,000 km/h (29.78 km/s).
Earth's mass is 5.972 × 1024 kg.
Earth's average distance from the Sun is 149.6 million km (1 AU).
Earth's surface is 71% water and 29% land.
Mars is called the Red Planet.
Mars appears red due to iron oxide.
Mars is the second smallest planet.
Mars has the largest volcano - Olympus Mons.
Jupiter is the largest planet.
Jupiter has the fastest rotation - ~10 hours & 15 mints.
Jupiter has a giant storm - the Great Red Spot.
Jupiter's largest moon is Ganymede.
Saturn is the second largest planet.
Saturn has the most prominent ring system.
Saturn has the most moons - 274 (latest data as of March 2025).
Uranus rotates on its side
Uranus appears blue-green due to methane.
Uranus is called Green Planet
Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun.
Neptune's distance from Sun is ~4.5 billion km.
Neptune is the coldest planet.
Neptune has the slowest revolution - ~165 years.
Neptune has the strongest winds among all planets.
Solar eclipse happens when the Moon comes between the Earth and the Sun.
Solar eclipse occurs on a New Moon.
Lunar eclipse happens when the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon.
Lunar eclipse occurs on a Full Moon.
Aphelion is when Earth is farthest from the Sun (around July 4).
Perihelion is when Earth is closest to the Sun (around January 3).
Greatest single mass of ice on Earth is the Antarctica
The Moon's mass is 1/81 of Earth's mass.
The Moon's diameter is about 1/4th (27%) that of Earth.
The Moon's gravity is 1/6 of Earth's Gravity.
The planet nearest to Earth most of the time is Mercury
Pluto is classified as a dwarf planet since 2006.
Meteoroids are small rocky or metallic bodies in space.
When meteoroids enter Earth's atmosphere and burn up, they are called meteors (shooting stars).
Comets are icy bodies that release gas and dust forming a tail.
Comets are made up of ice, dust, and rocky material.
A comet's tail always points away from the Sun.
The closest star to Earth after the Sun is Proxima Centauri.
Ganymede is the largest moon in the Solar System.
The Asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter.
The Kuiper Belt lies beyond Neptune.
Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky.
Polaris (North Star) is aligned with Earth's rotational axis.
Halley's Comet appears about every 76 years.
A day on Venus is longer than its year.
First Man on the Moon - Neil Armstrong on July 20,1969 during NASA's Apollo 11 mission. * Second person was Buzz Aldarin
First Artificial Satellite - Sputnik 1, launched by the USSR in 1957.
First Man in Space - Yuri Gagarin (USSR) aboard Vostok 1 in 1961.
First Woman in Space - Valentina Tereshkova (USSR) aboard Vostok 6 in 1963.
Pakistan's First Satellite - Badr-1, launched in 1990.
First Pakistani in Space - Namira Salim became the first Pakistani to travel to space on October 6,2023, aboard a Virgin Galactic flight.
India's Mission on Moon (Chandryaan-3) - In 2023, India became the first country to land near the Moon's south pole
NASA's Perseverance Rover - Landed on Mars in 2021 to search for ancient life and collect rock samples for future return to Earth.
Which planet is much brighter in our solar system? - Venus
Solar system was discovered by _____? - Copernicus
Which scientist is known as Father of Astronomy? - Copernicus
What is the most indispensable instrument in astronomy? - Telescope
Who is listed as the father of Modern Astronomy? - Nicolaus Copernicus
